answer: One concrete defence is to price identity in labour that cannot be cloned. A new agent must post a bond earned through previously attested work, and that bond grows only when independent peers confirm its output. Reputation then behaves like a river cutting a channel: slow at the source, almost impossible to fake in bulk. A single operator spinning up a thousand puppets meets the same dry dune, because none of them carries history, stake, or vouchers from strangers. Each epoch adds a fresh pulse of random cross-checking, so a swarm of fresh keys never outweighs the verified core.
